name: rectilinear-trap
description: A rectilinear ion trap in cross-section, in its transversal pulsed-extraction configuration: four flat plates around a square aperture, the front one split by an extraction slot, solved in the plane normal to the trap axis. This is the cross-section of the Stewart/Grinfeld Ion Processor (JASMS 2023) at r0 = 2 mm. Flat plates approximate a hyperbolic field far more crudely than round rods do, so with the trapping potentials applied the 12-pole content should be percent-level rather than parts per thousand; that is a property of the geometry, not a defect. With the extraction potentials applied the packet is pushed through the slot, and what the solve buys over the closed form is the field's departure from uniform across the packet - the turn-around-time formula assumes a uniform field and a slotted plate does not provide one.

inscribedRadius.description: Axis to the inner face of a plate, conventionally r0. The Ion Processor uses 2 mm in both the high- and low-pressure regions.

plateThickness.description: Thickness of each flat plate. Thicker plates deepen the slot and make the extraction field leak less.

cornerGap.description: Insulating gap at each corner, where the front and back plates stop short of the side plates. A real trap needs one; setting it near zero shorts adjacent electrodes together and the solve will say so through the maximum principle.

slotWidth.description: Width of the extraction slot in the front plate. The trade this parameter carries is the whole design: too narrow and the packet clips, too wide and the extraction field sags in the middle and stops being uniform.

pushPotential.description: Applied to the back plate during extraction. The Ion Processor pulses 500 to 1000 V transversally. This sets the extraction field and with it the turn-around time, which goes as one over it.

frontPotential.description: Applied to the slotted front plate.

sidePotential.description: Applied to both side plates. Zero during extraction; set to plus and minus a common value against the front and back plates to put the trap in its RF-analogue trapping configuration and inspect the multipole content.

driftLength.description: From the outer face of the front plate to the detector plane. Field-free to the extent the slot lets it be, which is the point of solving it rather than assuming it.

housingClearance.description: From the outermost electrode to the grounded domain boundary. The boundary is the housing, so this says how tightly the trap is enclosed.

cellsPerRadius.description: Grid cells across the inscribed radius. The slot and the corner gaps are the smallest features, so check that both still span several cells before trusting a coarse run.
